identity.title: Nucleic acid amplification testing for obligate intracellular and cell wall-deficient bacteria: from assay performance to clinical interpretation, a structured narrative review.

content.abstract: Obligate intracellular bacteria (Rickettsia, Orientia, Ehrlichia, Anaplasma, Coxiella, Chlamydia) and cell wall-deficient Mycoplasma species present profound diagnostic challenges due to their fastidious growth, low circulating burden, and genomic instability. Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests (NAATs) have revolutionized detection, yet critical gaps persist in distinguishing active infection from persistent DNA, standardizing cycle threshold interpretation, and integrating host-response biomarkers. This structured narrative review provides a comprehensive analysis of the complete diagnostic armamentarium for these pathogens. It is based on a reproducible, non-systematic literature survey and is not a PRISMA-compliant systematic review. We cover conventional methods (culture, serology), NAAT platforms (qPCR, digital PCR, isothermal amplification), and emerging technologies including CRISPR-Cas diagnostics, metagenomic sequencing, nanopore sequencing, biosensors, and host-response biomarker profiling. We introduce four conceptual frameworks: the "biological noise" paradigm reframing low-copy detection as a signal-to-noise challenge; a temporal-dynamic algorithm accounting for pathogen-specific detection windows; the "detection-disease disconnect" emphasizing clinical contextualization of NAAT positivity; and multi-analyte integration combining NAAT with viability markers and host inflammatory signatures. We also position these frameworks relative to prior diagnostic-interpretation theories, including STARD, QUADAS-2, MIQE, Bayesian pretest-posttest reasoning, Ct-value interpretation guidance, and host-response classifier frameworks. We compare ten clinically significant pathogens across technical and biological parameters, evaluate point-of-care deployment strategies, and address antimicrobial resistance testing. Performance metrics are presented as context-dependent estimates rather than fixed constants. The next frontier lies not in incremental assay improvements but in system-level integration of pathogen detection, viability assessment, host-response profiling, and clinical phenotyping, supported by artificial intelligence-enhanced interpretation and global standardization efforts.
